Design system: Obsidian, plus user-selectable Appearance

Decision (2026-11-05): Obsidian is the default look. Users can change it later in Settings › Appearance. The radial deck view from the "Signal" exploration ships as an Appearance option, not as a separate app style.

Design canvas: Soundboard — design directions → page Obsidian (chosen). The Appearance screen on that page is interactive.

Tokens: design/tokens/obsidian.tokens.json. The colour standard is OKLCH only, uses semantic tokens, and has one brand colour per product.

Obsidian in one paragraph

Obsidian is a precision instrument on true black. The waveform is the hero: lows, mids and highs are drawn as three overlaid bands in blue, orange and white. A beat grid, phrase markers ("DROP · 8 BARS") and a whole-track overview with sections and hot-cue ticks sit around it. All numbers use Geist Mono tabular figures; the UI uses Geist. The accent colour is reserved for "go" actions and states: Mix, playing, sync, the selected value. Everything else is neutral. Controls are drawn, not stock: arc knobs, segmented pickers, segmented meters, and pads with cue-colour bars. Corners are tight (4–8 px), dividers are hairlines, and there is no decorative gradient or glow.

The Appearance model

SettingOptions (default first)What it changes
ThemeOLED Black · Graphite · DaylightNeutral-to-semantic mapping (color-background … color-text-muted)
AccentVolt (lime) · Signal (pink) · Ice (cyan) · Ember (orange) · Violetcolor-primary / -hover / -active, the single brand family
Deck viewLinear · Radial · LanesWhich waveform component the deck renders
Waveform coloursSpectral · Accent · Monocolor-wave-low / -mid / -high
DensityComfortable · CompactSpacing scale and control sizes, with 44 pt minimum touch targets kept
Follow system light/darkoffSwitches OLED ↔ Daylight with the OS
Per-controller layoutsonRemembers deck view and density for each MIDI controller profile

Rules

  1. Components only read semantic tokens. A theme, accent or waveform choice only changes token values. No component has a branch per theme.
  2. One accent at a time. The accent replaces the brand family. Semantic colours (success, warning, error, info) and hot-cue colours never change with it, so meaning stays stable.
  3. Deck view is a component swap, not a skin. Linear, Radial and Lanes all take the same input: the three-band waveform bins, beat grid, phrases, cues and play position. They render it differently. Mixer, pads and transport don't change.
  4. Accessibility holds in every combination. Text tokens keep at least 4.5:1 against their surfaces in all three themes. Text on the accent uses color-on-primary (near-black), which clears 4.5:1 on all five accents at the 500 step. The radial view always shows BPM, time and phrase as text inside the ring, not only as graphics.
  5. Performance is protected. Changing appearance never touches the audio engine. Deck-view rendering budgets are the same: 120 Hz on ProMotion, and the waveform drawn on the GPU (Metal / Compose Canvas).

Code

  • design/tokens/generate.py writes ObsidianTokens.generated.swift from the JSON. Re-run it after any token change; a test fails if the Swift data drifts from the JSON.
  • SemanticPalette.resolve(_:) resolves references for one Appearance. Components read @Environment(\.obsidian) and use semantic colours only.
  • Waveform presets: Spectral, Deck tint (deck B overrides), High contrast, Accent, Mono, and Custom with guardrails: adjacent bands must differ by at least 0.12 OKLCH lightness. Mid is lifted first, then High falls back to white, and every adjustment is explained to the user.

Platform mapping

  • SwiftUI: AppearanceSettings (@Observable, persisted with @AppStorage) produces a Theme value injected through @Environment. Semantic colours are Color values built from OKLCH (converted to Display P3 at build time), resolved per theme and accent.
  • Compose: a SoundboardTheme(appearance) composable provides a SoundboardColors class through a CompositionLocal. Settings are stored in DataStore.
  • Sync: Appearance is part of the synced preferences, so the same look follows the user across devices. Per-controller layouts are stored per device.

What changed from earlier rounds

  • Round 1 felt too basic and Android-like: pill buttons, stock sliders, card stacks.
  • Its colours came from auto-generated ramps and looked muddy. Every colour is now chosen by hand.
  • Glass (vertical lanes) is kept as the Lanes deck view. Signal's ring is kept as Radial.
